heading: INT. COUNTY COURTHOUSE - JANITOR'S CLOSET OFF THE ATRIUM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. COUNTY COURTHOUSE - JANITOR'S CLOSET OFF THE ATRIUM - NIGHT
Mops, buckets, a bare bulb.
A cracked radio plays low jazz.
Shelving crowded with floor wax and light bulbs.
A WOMAN in a good wool suit sits on an overturned bucket.
She has the look of someone who has been crying and has stopped.
A leather briefcase rests on her knees.
At the door, an old man in coveralls leans on a push broom.
He is the night custodian, MORDECAI TILLMAN (70s, silver stubble, a ring of keys the size of a dinner plate).
Counselor, I don't mean to pry.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: Then don't.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: But it's a quarter to midnight, and you're in my closet.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: I needed a door that locked.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Mine does. From the outside.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: I noticed.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: He sets down the broom.
Pulls up a second bucket, upside down, and lowers himself onto it with a grunt.
I've worked this building forty-one years. I know the sound a person makes when they've lost.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: I haven't lost.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: No?
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: The verdict comes tomorrow.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Then why's your face look like that?
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: Because I know how it ends.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Do you now.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: My client did it, Mr. Tillman.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: I thought so.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: You thought so?
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: I clean the defendants' table. They leave things behind.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: She laughs, a sharp breath through her nose.
And what do they leave?
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Gum. Rosaries. Once, a gun, but that's another story.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: My name is Esperanza Calloway-Reyes. Not Counselor.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Pleased to meet you, Ms. Calloway-Reyes.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: I'm supposed to believe in him. That's the job.
units.name: ESPERANZA

units.text: And?
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: I did believe in him. Right up until the jury was seated.
units.name: ESPERANZA

units.text: Seems a late time to stop.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: It's the time I started noticing.
units.name: ESPERANZA

units.text: Silence.
The radio shifts to a slow saxophone.
Mordecai reaches over, turns it down.
Ms. Calloway-Reyes, you want my advice?
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: Do I have a choice?
units.name: ESPERANZA

units.text: No. But here it is. Go home. Sleep. Tomorrow, stand up and do the work.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: Even if I know he's guilty?
units.name: ESPERANZA

units.text: Especially then.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: She nods, slowly.
Stands.
Tucks the briefcase under her arm.
Thank you.
units.name: ESPERANZA

units.text: Don't mention it. I don't know anything.
units.name: MORDECAI

units.text: He opens the door.
She steps into the dark atrium, her heels echoing across the marble.
